headline: Wet, windy, and mild; a break Thursday, then more storms Friday through Sunday.
summary: Moist air from the Pacific has brought rain and high-elevation snow to western Washington, and a warm front is lifting north out of the region tonight. A cold front will stall offshore Wednesday into Thursday, and then a series of Pacific storms moves in from Friday through Sunday, with a brief break Monday before another front arrives Tuesday. For the Seattle area, Wednesday is mild, in the 60s, with strong south winds along the coast and in the north. The interior gets a break from rain Thursday. Friday through Sunday brings more lowland rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds, strongest on the coast. The Skokomish River in Mason County is running high and could flood again. Forecasters are fairly confident in the overall pattern, but the exact track of the storms could still shift.
changes: The weekend is now described as a series of Pacific storms rather than two separate systems, and the latest discussion adds a brief Monday break followed by another front Tuesday. The interior is also now expected to get a rain break on Thursday.
